assertions.name: kashaev_sum_confirms_numerically
assertions.source: Kashaev's sum at N = 32000, 64000, Richardson-extrapolated, against 3^{-1/4}

description: Derives c_sigma(4_1) = 3^{-1/4} and the power N^{3/2} by Laplace on Kashaev's one-variable sum, closing the knot side that qou-vdvS left open. Together with the link-side closed form this retires the 4_1 calibration: k = 2^{-1/2} is derived at both legs. Exhibits tau_DG as the Hessian of the Lobachevsky potential at the geometric saddle, and identifies why exactly two closed-form families exist — the two regular ideal polyhedra, with trace fields Q(sqrt-3) and Q(i). Nothing fitted; the value is predicted from the saddle and only confirmed numerically.

derivation.expansion: s_k = (N/pi) Lambda(theta) - (1/2) log(2 N sin theta) + O(1/N), theta = k pi/N — the same expansion verified for van der Veen's Lemma 3
derivation.saddle_condition: Lambda'(theta) = -log(2 sin theta) = 0, so 2 sin theta* = 1
derivation.volume: (2N/pi) Lambda(pi/6) = Vol N/(2 pi), Vol(4_1) = 4 Lambda(pi/6)
derivation.rigidity: in one variable the saddle condition IS 2 sin theta* = 1, so the Stirling factor is forced to 1 and c_sigma = |cot theta*|^{-1/2} = 3^{-1/4} with no freedom

tau_is_the_hessian.reading: the DG 1-loop invariant is the Hessian determinant of the Lobachevsky potential at the geometric saddle, divided by the Stirling factor; this is the smallest case where that can be seen explicitly

why_exactly_two_closed_form_families.principle: the saddle sits at a root-of-unity shape exactly for the regular ideal polyhedra, and then det(Hessian) is an algebraic number in a cyclotomic trace field

octahedral.tau: 2^{2n-2} |A|, A = n - m i in Z[i]

why_exactly_two_closed_form_families.why_no_third: those are the two imaginary quadratic fields with extra units — the two Bianchi cases. Q(zeta_5) is degree 4 and not imaginary quadratic, so there is no 5-fold regular ideal polyhedron tiling by the same route; see bean qou-dodK for the one candidate that does carry sqrt5, the Aitchison-Rubinstein dodecahedral knots
